name: FL-24
label: Safe D

key_factors: District's D+22 partisan lean makes a Republican win structurally improbable
Polymarket prices the Democrat at roughly 96 percent
Gilbert holds a clear fundraising edge over Brown despite $2.1M in outside spending against him
Open seat with no general-election polling leaves residual uncertainty
model.rationale: The district's 22-point Democratic lean, Gilbert's fundraising advantage, and market pricing near 96 percent all point to a comfortable Democratic hold despite Wilson's retirement. The unusually heavy outside spending opposing Gilbert is the one caution flag, but it is unlikely to overcome the seat's fundamentals.
model.watch: If the $2.1M in outside spending against Gilbert reflects a genuine Republican opening or an emerging candidate vulnerability rather than routine general-election activity, the margin could tighten.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Frederica Wilson (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Florida's 24th District, anchored in Miami-Dade County, leans heavily Democratic, and Frederica Wilson's retirement turns this into an open-seat contest rather than a true battleground. Democrat Oliver Gilbert has out-raised Republican Te Mayonna Brown and drawn substantial outside help, though outside groups have also spent heavily opposing him. No independent polls of the general election are available, and no expert raters have flagged the race as competitive.

Prediction markets put the Democratic candidate's chances around 96 percent, consistent with the district's roughly 22-point Democratic lean. With no incumbent on the ballot and no polling to lean on, some uncertainty remains, but the fundamentals — the partisan makeup of the electorate and the clear funding gap — favor Democrats to hold the seat comfortably in November.
